# T2.05b: bisecting the methods

`encode1` sends its buffer methods in a fixed order. `NVENC_VAR=upto=N` sends only the first N before `EXECUTE`, and
`bare` sends only the status buffer. 256x128 QP 26, setup as before:

| N | last method added | result | `ucode_error_status` |
|---|---|---|---|
| bare | `SET_OUT_ENC_STATUS` only | done in 0.7 ms, no channel error | 3 `E_PICSETUP_OFFSET` |
| 2 | `SET_PICTURE_INDEX`, `SET_OUT_ENC_STATUS` | done | 3 `E_PICSETUP_OFFSET` |
| 3 | `SET_IN_DRV_PIC_SETUP` | done | 14 `E_INPUT_HISTORY_OFFSET` |
| 4 | `SET_OUT_BITSTREAM` | done | 14 |
| 5 | `SET_IOHISTORY` | done | 13 `E_INPUT_BITSTREAM_OFFSET` (= input picture missing) |
| 6 | `SET_IN_CUR_PIC` (luma) | MMU fault (chroma base still 0) | - |
| 7 | `SET_IN_CUR_PIC_CHROMA_U` | **RC 47**, `error_status` 1, ucode 0 | 0 |
| 8-24 | recon, coloc, the 14 extra buffers | RC 47 | 0 |

Findings:
- The microcode runs, checks its buffers in order and reports clean errors (`error_status` 2 + code from
  `ERROR_CODES` in nvenc_drv.h), with the execute completing and the semaphore released. Our channel, methods and
  addresses are fine.
- **RC 47 starts as soon as the input picture is complete**, i.e. when the engine actually starts encoding. Leaving
  out recon, coloc or the extra buffers doesn't matter. The failure is in the encode itself: picture setup contents
  or the input/recon surfaces (T2.05c).
- `error_status` 1 with `ucode_error_status` 0 is a different kind of failure from the microcode's own checks
  (which use `error_status` 2). It looks like a hardware error/interrupt that the microcode passes to RM as an engine
  error (RC 47) instead of completing.
- The earlier "bad magic changes nothing" result fits: the stage-3 runs show the magic is accepted (the check moves
  on to the history buffer), and a wrong magic gives the same RC 47 because the hardware error comes first or the
  magic isn't checked on this path.
